questions.q: Why does this lesson say catalogs are the most realistic place to get a true single pane of glass across Azure and AWS, compared to identity or policy?
options: A catalog's job is describing metadata, and metadata doesn't care which cloud physically stores the data — unlike identity and policy, which are separate control planes
AWS and Azure use the exact same catalog software by default
Catalogs are easier to build than any other governance tool
Identity and policy tools do not exist on AWS
questions.explain: Entra ID/AWS IAM and Azure Policy/AWS Organizations are genuinely separate control planes with no shared data model, but metadata about an asset is the same concept regardless of which cloud stores the asset.

questions.q: How does Microsoft Purview's multicloud scanning connector authenticate to read an Amazon S3 bucket, per this lesson?
options: Through a federated IAM role trust and an External ID — not a stored AWS access key
By storing a permanent AWS access key and secret in Purview
By requiring the AWS account owner to manually approve every single scan
Purview cannot connect to AWS S3 at all
questions.explain: An AWS IAM role trusts Purview's Microsoft account ID, and an External ID (a shared secret) ensures only Purview's actual scanner can assume that role — no long-lived AWS credential is stored.

questions.q: What is the External ID's purpose in the AWS role trust, according to this lesson?
options: It ensures only the intended trusted party (Purview) can assume the role, not just anyone who learns the Microsoft account ID
It is the AWS bucket's public URL
It replaces the need for any IAM role entirely
It is a random value with no security function
questions.explain: Knowing the Microsoft account ID alone isn't enough to assume the role — the External ID acts as a shared secret that must also match, preventing a 'confused deputy' style misuse of the trust.

questions.q: Once an AWS S3 source is scanned, how do its assets appear in the Purview Unified Catalog, per this lesson?
options: Exactly like any Azure asset — filterable by asset type, with the same classification facets, in the same search results
In a completely separate catalog that cannot be searched together with Azure assets
Only as raw file names with no classification information
They do not appear in the catalog at all, only in a separate report
questions.explain: A steward can search the catalog and get Azure and AWS results in the same list, without needing to know which cloud the data physically lives on.

questions.q: Does cataloging both an AWS source and an Azure source automatically give you lineage between them, per this lesson?
options: No — lineage across clouds requires the pipeline tool moving the data (such as Data Factory) to itself be integrated with and report to Purview
Yes — cataloging both sources automatically traces every hop between them
Yes, but only for buckets smaller than 1 GB
Lineage is not a concept that applies to cloud storage
questions.explain: Scanning both sources independently catalogs each side, but doesn't connect the dots between them unless something in the middle — the actual pipeline — explicitly reports that connection.
